# Chest Pain Work-up Predicate Engine

*Working Draft — October 2026*

---

## Overview

![][image1]

This document describes the design of the chest pain predicate engine for life underwriting. The engine finds chest pain applicants whose care is an emergency department (ED) work-up. It separates these applicants from applicants who have other care that explains the chest pain.

The engine uses a cohort of 139,416 chest pain patients. A data method groups these patients by the care they receive. The method found 8 care patterns. The ED work-up is care pattern c3. It has 17,250 patients (12.4%). The 7 other care patterns are the comparison group.

Today every `dx_9487` (atypical chest pain) case goes to manual review at RUW. This engine is a candidate to narrow the cases that go to manual review. It is a draft and has no validation yet.

---

## Predicates and Composites

This section defines the parts of the chest pain predicate engine. It covers the atomic predicates and the composites that combine them into named clinical patterns. This section contains no underwriting logic. Clinicians and medical reviewers use it to check that the definitions agree with established chest pain care.

Each predicate uses a list of codes. For example, the troponin list holds every troponin code. The code table shows all codes of all lists: [full list of codes](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1B57C72qmkEQowD4u9zQ9eIB0v9UOowiV/view?usp=sharing).

### Atomic Predicates

A predicate answers one question about the event history of an applicant. It returns true or false. Atomic predicates check directly against raw event attributes. The code and the date are attributes of one event.

**Chest pain present.** The applicant has at least one chest pain event. The list holds chest pain, precordial pain, chest pain on breathing, and pain of the space between the ribs. Chest pain has many causes. Presence alone does not show the care pathway.

`chest_pain_present = event IS chest pain diagnosis`

**First chest pain date.** This is the date of the first chest pain event of the applicant. The engine measures all other dates from this date.

`first_chest_pain_date = MIN(event_date) over chest pain events`

**Troponin present.** The applicant has at least one troponin test. Troponin is a blood test for injury to the heart muscle. The data does not show the type of test. A high-sensitivity test and a standard test look the same.

`troponin_present = event IS troponin test`

**Chest X-ray present.** The applicant has at least one chest X-ray. The list holds X-rays of 1, 2, 3, and 4 or more views.

`cxr_present = event IS chest X-ray`

**Lipase present.** The applicant has at least one lipase test. Lipase is a blood test for the pancreas. Doctors also use it for abdominal pain. A lipase test alone does not show chest pain care.

`lipase_present = event IS lipase test`

**IV push present.** The applicant has at least one IV push injection. An IV push puts a drug into a vein with a syringe. The list holds the first drug and each additional drug. Doctors use an IV push for many complaints. An IV push alone does not show chest pain care.

`iv_push_present = event IS IV push (first drug OR each additional drug)`

**Service in window.** A work-up service is troponin, chest X-ray, lipase, or IV push. A service is in the window when its event is not more than 1 day before or after a chest pain event. The window is 1 day.

`workup_window_days = 1`

`<service>_in_window = <service>_present AND EXISTS chest pain event date d, service event date e with |e - d| <= workup_window_days`

The 4 predicates are `troponin_in_window`, `cxr_in_window`, `lipase_in_window`, and `iv_push_in_window`.

The window is the same for all services. For each service, the median first event is on the same day as the first chest pain. 21% to 34% of the patients with a service had it before the first chest pain. The window has two sides, because an ED test sometimes has a date 1 day before the chest pain claim. The value of 1 day is a draft. It has no calibration yet.

---

### Composites

A composite combines atomic predicates, or other composites, into a named clinical pattern. Composites are in three groups: work-up services, work-up sequences, and the ED work-up pattern.

#### Work-up services

These composites count the work-up services of an applicant.

**Work-up service count.** This is the number of the 4 work-up services that are in the window for the applicant.

`workup_service_count = troponin_in_window + cxr_in_window + lipase_in_window + iv_push_in_window`

**Work-up services.** The applicant has 3 or more of the 4 work-up services in the window. The composite stays true when the claims do not show one service. The value 3 is a draft. It has no calibration yet.

`composite_workup_services = workup_service_count >= 3`

#### Work-up sequences

A sequence is a list of events in a fixed order. Other events between the steps do not break the sequence. Every sequence starts at a chest pain event. The last step is not more than 1 day after that chest pain event. A step is true for any code of its list.

The data method found these 3 sequences. They are the 3 sequences that are most specific to the ED work-up. Each sequence has 4 steps. The ECG (electrocardiogram) is a heart tracing. The CMP (comprehensive metabolic panel) is a blood chemistry test. The CBC is the complete blood count.

**Sequence A.** The applicant has a chest pain event, then a chest X-ray, then a troponin test, then a CMP test.

`composite_seq_cxr_trop_cmp = chest_pain -> cxr -> troponin -> cmp`

**Sequence B.** The applicant has a chest pain event, then an ECG, then a troponin test, then a CMP test. The ECG is a step in this sequence only. It is not a work-up service.

`composite_seq_ecg_trop_cmp = chest_pain -> ecg -> troponin -> cmp`

**Sequence C.** The applicant has a chest pain event, then a troponin test, then a CMP test, then a CBC test.

`composite_seq_trop_cmp_cbc = chest_pain -> troponin -> cmp -> cbc`

**Work-up sequence.** The applicant has at least one of the sequences A, B, or C.

`composite_workup_sequence = composite_seq_cxr_trop_cmp OR composite_seq_ecg_trop_cmp OR composite_seq_trop_cmp_cbc`

#### Same-day order

Claims have a date and no time. The engine puts the events of one day in a fixed order. The order is diagnosis, then procedure, then lab test. Lab tests follow the order of their code ID: troponin, then CMP, then CBC.

The 3 sequences are mostly same-day patterns. Their support falls below half when each step needs a later day. The order of same-day steps is therefore a rule. It is not the clock time.

#### ED work-up pattern

**ED work-up pattern.** The applicant has chest pain, 3 or more work-up services in the window, and at least one work-up sequence. This pattern shows the type of care. It does not show a diagnosis. A normal test result also gives this pattern. The predicates test that a service happened, not the result.

`composite_ed_workup_pattern = chest_pain_present AND composite_workup_services AND composite_workup_sequence`

---

## Population Coverage

Counts come from the chest pain cohort of 139,416 patients. Percentages are patient-level. The tables come from the k=8 run of the data method (`nmf_k8_chestpain_AHA`). The extract carries event dates. The engine has no measured rate for any predicate or composite yet.

### Cohort composition

Each patient is in the care pattern with the highest weight for that patient.

| Care pattern | Name | Patients | % cohort |
| :---- | :---- | ----: | ----: |
| c0 | outpatient check-up and elective cardiac testing | 31,113 | 22.3% |
| c1 | prescriptions for acute and chronic illness | 24,606 | 17.6% |
| c2 | women's health and urinary tract | 16,770 | 12.0% |
| **c3** | **ED work-up** | **17,250** | **12.4%** |
| c4 | stomach and bowel work-up and cancer screening | 8,409 | 6.0% |
| c5 | muscle and bone care and physical therapy | 19,127 | 13.7% |
| c6 | nutrition and hormone blood tests | 10,987 | 7.9% |
| c7 | acute respiratory infection | 11,154 | 8.0% |

### Predicate rates

The rates are for patients of care pattern c3. They count a service at any time, not only in the window.

| Service | Patients with the service | Median day against first chest pain | Share that had it before first chest pain |
| :---- | ----: | :---- | ----: |
| Troponin | 81% | same day | 21% |
| Chest X-ray | 86% | same day | 33% |
| Lipase | 59% | same day | 34% |
| IV push, first drug | 66% | same day | 33% |
| IV push, each additional drug | 55% | same day | 34% |

### Sequence rates

The shares count the steps in this order at any time. They do not use the 1-day limit. The other care patterns are a random sample of 1,500 patients.

| Sequence | Patients of c3 | Patients of the other care patterns | Times as common | Held-out check |
| :---- | ----: | ----: | ----: | :---- |
| A. Chest pain, chest X-ray, troponin, CMP | 59.4% | 24.4% | 2.4 | passed |
| B. Chest pain, ECG, troponin, CMP | 64.9% | 26.7% | 2.4 | passed |
| C. Chest pain, troponin, CMP, CBC | 62.8% | 25.5% | 2.4 | passed |

The held-out check repeats the test on random halves of the patients, in 40 runs. All 3 sequences passed. About 1 in 4 patients of the other care patterns also has each sequence. The window and the rule of 3 services narrow the match.
